title: Work IQ: REST endpoint tools for agents
summary: The roadmap facts and documented background controls are largely accurate, including the beta spending-policy endpoint flagged by the pre-check. The risk section incorrectly says the roadmap does not associate its phases with dates, and the metered cost rating goes beyond the feature-specific billing evidence the briefing says is available.

claims.quote: Enable agents to use supported REST endpoints as tools through governed Work IQ integrations.

claims.claim: Learn does not yet describe this roadmap capability specifically.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "REST endpoint tools"; opened Work IQ overview, API overview and MCP management reference. Found remote API tool creation, but no explicit identification with this roadmap item.
claims.fix: Narrow 'Learn does not describe it yet' to 'Learn does not explicitly identify this roadmap item. Its Work IQ overview search excerpt describes custom MCP servers supporting arbitrary REST endpoints, while the fetched overview describes 10 generic tools; the relationship to this item is not stated.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq#skills-and-tools alongside the existing MCP management reference.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not identified which REST endpoints are supported by this roadmap feature.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "REST" "tools" "policy" registry supported endpoints credentials; opened Work IQ overview, API overview and MCP management reference. No feature-specific endpoint list found.

claims.claim: The registration and approval route for this roadmap feature is not explicitly identified.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "REST endpoint tools"; opened Work IQ overview, registry management and MCP management reference. Remote API tool creation is documented, but its identity with this roadmap feature is not stated.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not specified the credentials carried by REST endpoint tool calls for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "REST" "tools" "policy" registry supported endpoints credentials; opened API overview and MCP management reference. Delegated Work IQ authentication is documented, but no credential model for this named roadmap feature was found.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not explicitly specified where this feature's tools appear or whether they join the existing Work IQ MCP server.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "REST endpoint tools"; opened Work IQ overview, Agent 365 server options and MCP management reference. No explicit mapping from this roadmap item to a server or maker experience found.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP is a single MCP endpoint with 10 generic tools.
claims.quote: A single MCP endpoint with 10 generic tools.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP uses a Rego-based policy engine to enforce request-time rules.
claims.quote: A Rego-based policy engine enforces detailed, context-aware rules on every request.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; controls[2]
claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy blocks mutation operations by default, including create, update, delete and actions such as sending email.
claims.quote: By default, mutation operations aren't allowed for safety. This restriction includes create, update, delete, and action requests that modify data, such as sending email.

claims.claim: Documented Work IQ requests run in the context of the signed-in user.
claims.quote: Requests run in the context of the signed-in user.

claims.claim: Work IQ uses Microsoft Entra ID delegated authentication.
claims.quote: Work IQ uses Microsoft Entra ID delegated authentication.

claims.claim: Work IQ does not support application-only authentication.
claims.quote: Application-only authentication isn't supported.

claims.claim: Approval of a developer-registered MCP server and Microsoft Entra consent are separate steps.
claims.quote: Approval in this flow applies to the selected MCP server registration, not to a whole plugin package that uses the server. Granting the required Microsoft Entra consent is a separate step.

claims.claim: The Work IQ overview says every tool invocation is logged and evaluated.
claims.quote: Every tool invocation is logged and evaluated, enabling auditability, usage analytics, rate limiting, and real-time compliance enforcement across agents and data sources.

claims.claim: The roadmap lists Preview and General Availability without saying which applies when.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "October CY2026", "targetDate": "November CY2026", "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]
claims.fix: Replace 'The roadmap lists both Preview and General Availability without saying which applies when.' with 'The roadmap targets preview for October CY2026 and release for November CY2026, while still listing the status as In development.'

claims.claim: Tools registry availability can vary by tenant, region, rollout, licensing, administrator approval and organisational policy.
claims.quote: What appears in the registry and in agent-building experiences can vary by tenant, region, rollout status, licensing, administrator approval, and organizational policy.

claims.claim: A registered MCP server can be blocked tenant-wide under Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Registry > MCP server > Block, disabling its exposed tools.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Tools, and then select the Registry tab. ... Select an MCP server from the list to open its overview pane. ... Select Block to restrict the server across your organization ... Blocking an MCP server disables all the tools it exposes.

claims.claim: No API for the registry's server-blocking action is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Agent 365 Tools registry block MCP server individual tools management API PowerShell; "MCP" "block" "registry" "Graph" API Agent 365 tools. Opened registry management; read CLI reference excerpt removing develop-mcp block. No equivalent API call found.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Individual supported MCP tools can be toggled under Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Registry > MCP server > Tools > Enabled or Disabled > Save.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Tools, and then select the Registry tab. ... Select an MCP server ... Select the Tools tab. ... an Enabled or Disabled toggle. ... Select Save to apply your changes, or Discard changes to cancel.

claims.claim: No equivalent API for the registry's individual-tool toggles is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Agent 365 Tools registry block MCP server individual tools management API PowerShell; "MCP" "block" "registry" "Graph" API Agent 365 tools. Opened registry management; read Azure API Management integration excerpts. No equivalent registry API found.

claims.claim: Individual-tool control is rolling out and supports only specific MCP server types registered on Agent 365.
claims.quote: Tool-level granular control is rolling out to tenants and supports only specific types of MCP servers registered on Agent 365.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy is managed under Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Policy, when that tab is available.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select Agents > Tools. ... In the tools registry, select Work IQ MCP. ... On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the Policy tab when it's available.

claims.claim: No Work IQ MCP policy configuration API is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ MCP" policy configuration API PowerShell tenant settings; "Work IQ" "policy" "GET" "PATCH". Opened policy governance; read MCP overview and tool reference excerpts. No policy configuration endpoint or cmdlet found.

claims.claim: Initial Work IQ MCP policy control is tenant-level, with an on/off setting.
claims.quote: In the initial release, Work IQ MCP provides tenant-level policy control. In the Microsoft 365 admin center, tenant administrators can turn Work IQ MCP policy on or off for the tenant.

claims.claim: A saved Work IQ MCP policy change can take up to 24 hours to apply across the tenant.
claims.quote: After you save the setting, it can take up to 24 hours for the policy change to apply across your tenant.

claims.claim: Per-user, per-app and per-agent policy templates are not part of the initial Work IQ MCP control surface.
claims.quote: Per-user, per-app, per-agent, or scenario-specific policy templates aren't part of the initial policy control surface.

claims.where: front matter: cost; rationale: cost; controls[3].note
claims.claim: The feature is assigned the factual cost rating variable even though the page leaves its metering unconfirmed and establishes only the surrounding product's meter.
claims.quote: cost: "variable"; "whether REST endpoint tool calls are metered is not published." The assessment scale defines variable as metered and requires rating the change, not the surrounding product.
claims.fix: Set cost to 'low' and replace the cost rationale with 'Low. The only established cost of this roadmap change is administrative review time; licensing and metering for REST endpoint tools are not yet published.' Retain the separately qualified Work IQ API billing background.
